primitives.name: Postulate Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The typical procedure in science is to adopt a postulate tentatively, deduce one or more of its logical implications concerning observable phenomena, and then check the validity of the deductions by observation.
primitives.assumptions: Postulate is logically consistent; deductions are valid; observations are accurate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D ≠ O, indicating falsification or need for modification.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian update P(D|O) ≈ P(O|D)P(D)/P(O); GSE state transition on ¬(D ↔ O).

primitives.name: Deduction Conflict Resolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the deduction is in genuine disagreement with observation, the postulate must be either abandoned or so modified that it implies no such conflicting statement.
primitives.assumptions: Conflict is genuine and not due to measurement error.

layer2.mapping: GSI: rejection sampling or reparameterization; GSE: belief revision kernel.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core structure of scientific theory is a recursive feedback loop: postulate generation, deduction of consequences, empirical testing, and adjustment. This mirrors Bayesian inference where priors (postulates) are updated through likelihoods (deductions) against evidence (observations). Each iteration increases credibility but never achieves certainty, reflecting the probabilistic nature of knowledge. In GSI, this manifests as dynamic belief updating using conformal prediction. In GSE, it becomes a state machine where each validation step modifies internal beliefs. The failure mode occurs when deductions are misaligned with observations, triggering conflict resolution. The mathematical duality lies in the symmetry between logical implication and probabilistic conditioning, both requiring consistency across domains.
